installation.note: whoami is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: whoami (who am I) displays the username of the current user. It's a simple utility for confirming your current user identity. Useful in scripts or when switching users to verify which user you're operating as.
when_to_use: Use in scripts to get current user
Confirm which user you're logged in as

syntax.description: Display the current username. No arguments required.

misconceptions.title: whoami shows full user info
misconceptions.misconception: whoami displays full user information like id command
misconceptions.reality: whoami only returns the username. Use id command to see user ID, group ID, and groups.
misconceptions.tip: whoami = just username. Use id for full user identity information (UID, GID, groups).

misconceptions.title: whoami shows original user with sudo
misconceptions.misconception: whoami shows original user when using sudo
misconceptions.reality: whoami shows effective user (root with sudo). Use $USER or $LOGNAME for original username when using sudo.
misconceptions.tip: whoami shows effective user (root with sudo). Use $USER environment variable for original user.

common_pitfalls.description: Expecting whoami to show UID, GID, or groups
common_pitfalls.solution: Use id command for full user information (UID, GID, groups). whoami only returns username.

common_pitfalls.description: whoami returns root when using sudo, not original user
common_pitfalls.solution: Use $USER or $LOGNAME environment variable for original username when using sudo. whoami shows effective user.

related_commands.relationship: Full user info; whoami shows name, id shows UID/GID/groups
related_commands.description: Display full user identity (UID, GID, groups)

related_commands.relationship: Logged in users; whoami shows current, who shows all
related_commands.description: Show all currently logged in users

related_commands.relationship: User info and activity; more detailed than whoami
related_commands.description: Show who is logged in and what they're doing

related_commands.relationship: User groups; whoami shows user, groups shows group memberships
related_commands.description: Display groups the current user belongs to

best_practices: Use whoami in scripts to get current username: USER=$(whoami)
Use id command for full user information (UID, GID, groups)
Remember: whoami shows effective user (root with sudo), use $USER for original user
Perfect for conditional checks in scripts based on username
Use for debugging permission issues - verify which user you're running as
performance_tips: whoami is instant - very fast command
Lightweight compared to id command - use when you only need username

additional_notes.simple_output: whoami returns only username - clean output perfect for scripts
additional_notes.sudo_context: Returns root when using sudo (effective user), not original user
additional_notes.script_usage: Common in scripts: USER=$(whoami) or if [ "$(whoami)" = "root" ]
additional_notes.alternative: Use $USER environment variable for similar functionality (but may not exist in all shells)
additional_notes.full_info: For full user information (UID, GID, groups), use id command instead
